_meta.source: MOE Full Subject-Based Banding subject offerings and SEAB syllabus lists, cross-read against school Sec 2 subject selection briefings
_meta.notes: Schools do not all offer every subject, and not every subject is offered at every level in every school. Availability here is the national picture, not a promise about any one school. Items marked provisional could not be read from a primary MOE or SEAB page in the session that built this file. See OPEN_QUESTIONS.md.

G1.label: G1
G1.name: General 1
G1.plain: Builds the foundation of a subject with a lot of hands on, practical work. Closest to what used to be called Normal Technical.
G1.grading: Graded A to E, like the old N(T) Level.

G2.label: G2
G2.name: General 2
G2.plain: Covers the subject in real depth at a steadier pace. Closest to what used to be called Normal Academic.
G2.grading: Graded 1 to 6, like the old N(A) Level.

G3.label: G3
G3.name: General 3
G3.plain: The most demanding version of the subject, covering the most ground fastest. Closest to what used to be called Express.
G3.grading: Graded A1 to 9, like the old O Level.

movement.headline: Your levels are not fixed.
movement.body: Students move subjects up and down a level during secondary school. It happens at the end of Sec 1, at the end of Sec 2, and for some subjects into Sec 3. Schools look at how you did across the year, not one paper. If you want to move a subject up, the conversation to have is with the teacher who teaches it, and the term to have it in is the one you are in now.

groups.label: Everyone takes these
groups.note: English, your Mother Tongue and Mathematics are compulsory. The choice is the level, not whether.

groups.label: More Mathematics
groups.note: Optional, and only worth taking if you actually like the subject.

groups.label: Science
groups.note: You take at least one. How many and in what shape is the choice.

groups.label: Humanities
groups.note: You take at least one. At G2 and G3 this normally means Social Studies plus one elective.

groups.label: Electives
groups.note: Where your school's offer matters most. Ask what yours actually runs.

subjects.name: English Language
subjects.doing: You read things you did not choose, work out what the writer is really doing, and then write and speak clearly enough that someone else can follow you.
subjects.likeIf: you notice when something is worded to persuade you, and you like being the one who can explain it back.
showsUp: Every post secondary route asks for it, without exception
Nursing, law, teaching, communications, anything client facing
Every job interview you will ever sit

subjects.name: Mother Tongue Language
subjects.doing: You read, write and hold conversations in Chinese, Malay or Tamil, including about things that are not easy to say.
subjects.likeIf: you like being able to move between two worlds, or you want to talk properly with your grandparents.
showsUp: Counts as the language in the JC aggregate
Regional business, media, translation, social work
Any workplace that serves Singapore as it actually is

subjects.name: Higher Mother Tongue
subjects.doing: The same language taken further, with more literature and harder writing.
subjects.likeIf: the language is a strength and you want to keep it that way.
showsUp: Can count toward JC admission
Language teaching, media, translation
Universities in the region

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.doing: You learn to handle number, shape, chance and change, and to notice when an answer is nonsense.
subjects.likeIf: you like a problem that has a definite answer and a route you can check.
showsUp: Almost every polytechnic and ITE course sets a Mathematics requirement
Engineering, finance, data, trades, logistics
Reading a payslip, a loan, or a news chart without being fooled

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics
subjects.doing: A second, harder Mathematics running alongside the first. Calculus, trigonometry, algebra taken much further.
subjects.likeIf: Mathematics is the subject you would do anyway, not the one you are enduring.
showsUp: Expected for JC science and some engineering routes
Engineering and computing diplomas
Makes first year of a technical course much less painful
subjects.caution: Taking this to look strong, while it drags three other subjects down, is a bad trade. Take it because you like it.

subjects.name: Science
subjects.doing: One combined science, taught with your hands as much as your head. You build, test, measure and find out why it did not work.
subjects.likeIf: you would rather find out by doing it than by reading about it.
showsUp: Nitec engineering, facility and health science courses
Aerospace, electrical, precision engineering trades
Any job where you have to work out why the machine stopped

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.doing: You work out why things move, heat up, light up and fall over, and then prove it with a measurement.
subjects.likeIf: you take things apart, or you want to know what is actually happening inside them.
showsUp: Engineering diplomas and degrees
Aviation, marine, energy, built environment
Anything with a motor, a circuit or a structure in it

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.doing: You find out what things are made of and what happens when you put them together, mostly by putting them together.
subjects.likeIf: you like a practical where the result is visible and you have to explain it.
showsUp: Pharmaceutical and chemical engineering, food science
Nursing and the allied health routes
Singapore's chemicals industry on Jurong Island

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.doing: You study living things at every scale, from a cell to an ecosystem, and how they go wrong.
subjects.likeIf: you are curious about bodies, disease, food or the environment.
showsUp: Nursing, biomedical science, veterinary and health routes
Food science, environmental and marine work
Any conversation with a doctor about your own body

subjects.name: Combined Science
subjects.doing: Two sciences in one subject, usually Physics with Chemistry or Chemistry with Biology. Broader than one science, lighter than two.
subjects.likeIf: you want to keep science open without giving it two of your subject slots.
showsUp: Meets the science requirement for most polytechnic courses
Health, engineering and applied science diplomas
Keeps several doors open while you decide
subjects.caution: Some polytechnic and JC courses ask specifically for a single science. Check the course, not the rumour.

subjects.name: Humanities
subjects.doing: You look at how Singapore and the world got to be the way they are, and practise arguing about it with evidence.
subjects.likeIf: you have opinions about why things are unfair and want better reasons for them.
showsUp: Service, retail, hospitality and community roles
Any work where you deal with people who are not like you
Understanding the news well enough to argue back

subjects.name: Social Studies
subjects.doing: You examine how Singapore is governed, how societies hold together or come apart, and how to weigh evidence you did not choose.
subjects.likeIf: you want to understand why policy is the way it is rather than just complain about it.
showsUp: Paired with a humanities elective at G2 and G3
Public service, law, social work, journalism
Voting, and knowing what you are voting about
subjects.note: At G2 and G3, Social Studies is normally taken together with one humanities elective as a single Humanities subject.

subjects.name: History
subjects.doing: You work from sources that disagree with each other and build an argument that holds up.
subjects.likeIf: you like an argument, and you want to know who benefits from the version you were told.
showsUp: Law, policy, heritage, teaching, journalism
Any degree that grades you on essays
Reading a headline and asking who wrote it and why

subjects.name: Geography
subjects.doing: You study why people, water, weather, money and cities end up where they do, with fieldwork and real data.
subjects.likeIf: you like maps, patterns, and being outside collecting something.
showsUp: Urban planning, environmental science, logistics
Climate and sustainability work, which is growing fast here
Understanding why your neighbourhood floods

subjects.name: Literature in English
subjects.doing: You read novels, plays and poems closely enough to say something about them that is not obvious.
subjects.likeIf: you have ever argued about what a film really meant.
showsUp: Law, teaching, communications, media, publishing
Any degree that grades you on essays
Being the person in the room who reads people well

subjects.name: Art
subjects.doing: You make work, defend it, and learn to look at other people's work properly.
subjects.likeIf: you already make things in your own time.
showsUp: Design, media and animation diplomas
NAFA and LASALLE under the University of the Arts Singapore
Portfolio based admission, where what you have made counts

subjects.name: Design and Technology
subjects.doing: You are given a real problem, and you design, build and test a thing that solves it.
subjects.likeIf: you would rather be holding a tool than a highlighter.
showsUp: Engineering, product design and built environment diplomas
ITE engineering and facility technology courses
Making the thing, not just the slide about the thing

subjects.name: Nutrition and Food Science
subjects.doing: You study what food is made of and what it does in a body, then cook and test it.
subjects.likeIf: you cook, or you want to know what is actually in what you eat.
showsUp: Food science, nutrition and culinary diplomas
Hospitality, health promotion, food manufacturing
Singapore's food security and alternative protein work

subjects.name: Food and Consumer Education
subjects.doing: You plan, cost, prepare and evaluate real meals, and learn to run a household budget.
subjects.likeIf: you want skills you will use next week, not in ten years.
showsUp: ITE culinary, hospitality and food service courses
Working kitchens across Singapore
Feeding yourself properly for the rest of your life

subjects.name: Music
subjects.doing: You perform, compose, and learn to hear what is going on inside a piece of music.
subjects.likeIf: you already play, write or produce something.
showsUp: Music and audio production diplomas
NAFA, LASALLE and the Yong Siew Toh Conservatory
Sound design, live events, teaching

subjects.name: Principles of Accounts
subjects.doing: You learn how money moving through a business is recorded, and how to read whether it is doing well.
subjects.likeIf: you like things to balance and you are patient about detail.
showsUp: Accountancy, banking and business diplomas
Running your own thing without being cheated
Finance, which is a very large employer here

subjects.name: Computing
subjects.doing: You write programs, work with data, and learn why software breaks.
subjects.likeIf: you like building something that does not exist yet and debugging it at midnight.
showsUp: Information technology, cybersecurity and data diplomas
Every industry, because software is in all of them now
Making your own tools instead of waiting for one

subjects.name: Elements of Business Skills
subjects.doing: You learn how a small business actually runs: serving customers, handling money, keeping records.
subjects.likeIf: you want to work with people and you like being useful straight away.
showsUp: ITE business, retail and service courses
Retail, hospitality and service work across Singapore
Running a stall, a shop or a service of your own

subjects.name: Exercise and Sports Science
subjects.doing: You study how the body performs, trains and recovers, and test it on real athletes, including yourself.
subjects.likeIf: sport is a serious part of your life and you want to understand it properly.
showsUp: Sport and exercise science diplomas
Coaching, physiotherapy, sports management
Republic Polytechnic and the Singapore Sports School routes

subjects.name: Drama
subjects.doing: You devise, rehearse and perform work, and learn to analyse why a piece of theatre lands.
subjects.likeIf: you are willing to be watched while you get it wrong.
showsUp: Performing arts and media diplomas
LASALLE, NAFA, School of the Arts
Teaching, events, and any job that needs presence

subjects.name: Electronics
subjects.doing: You build and fault find real circuits, and learn what each component is doing.
subjects.likeIf: you like a soldering iron and a problem that can be traced.
showsUp: ITE electronics and electrical engineering courses
Semiconductor and precision engineering, both large here
Fixing things other people throw away
